chunks: And it is narrated from Abū Hāshim al-Jaʿfarī, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who has a mamlūk who has run away from him: is it permissible for him to free him in the kaffārah of ẓihār? He said: “There is no harm in it, so long as he has not come to know of his death.”

key_terms.أَبَقَ: ran away or absconded from his owner
key_terms.الظِّهَارِ: the pre-Islamic form of injurious spousal declaration that requires expiation
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible
key_terms.يُعْتِقَهُ: to set him free or emancipate him

ai.seo_question: Can a runaway slave be freed as kaffarah for zihar?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the freeing of a runaway slave as expiation for ẓihār. The Imam عليه السلام permits it as long as the owner has not learned that the slave has died, indicating that the slave’s legal existence remains operative until death is known.
